answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy works like an orchard, not an open canyon: entry is gated by proof-of-work and identity costs, so flooding in is expensive, while established trees earn reputation slowly. Newcomers start with locked, low-spendable stakes and only gain standing after peers attest their graded work across epochs. Value flows like opal in stone — thin and rare, so faking dozens of identities pays far less than building one credible agent.
